scale.source: CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000000: "bir milyard"; CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000000000: "bir trilyon": the word for 10^12 is the short-scale "trilyon"; 10^9 has its own word.

space_groups.source: CLDR 48 az groups digits with ".", so a space between digit strings separates two numbers.

fraction_agreement.source: Wiktionary, "mənfi" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-az-mənfi.wikitext): "mənfi beş dərəcə soyuq", minus five degrees of cold: the noun after a count stays singular ("beş dərəcə"), so a part word does too.

scale_noun_agrees.source: Wiktionary, "mənfi" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-az-mənfi.wikitext): "mənfi beş dərəcə soyuq": the noun after a count stays singular ("beş dərəcə"); so CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1000000: "bir milyon" and CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 2000000: "iki milyon" use the same scale word.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: No plural scale word is listed; the setting matters for no entry.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 25: "iyirmi beş": the words follow each other with a space.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 125: "bir yüz iyirmi beş": the words follow each other with a space.

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 2500: "iki min beş yüz": the words follow each other with a space.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: No joiner stands after the thousands (joiner_between_groups is never): CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1500: "bir min beş yüz"; CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1020: "bir min iyirmi".

ordinal_style.source: Only the last word of an ordinal takes the ordinal suffix: CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-ordinal, ICU 78 rendering of 25: "iyirmi beşinci".

inflection_position.source: A case ending goes on the last word of the number and closes it: Wiktionary, "-da" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-az--da.wikitext): "Form of -də after the vowels A / I / O / U"; Wiktionary, "-dan" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-az--dan.wikitext): "Form of -dən after the vowels A / I / O / U"; Wiktionary, "-ə" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-az--ə.wikitext): "{{az-suffix-forms|a=a|ə=ə|v=y}}": "to (puts the word into the dative case)", "y" after a vowel.

dotted_i.source: Wikipedia, "Turkish alphabet" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Turkish_alphabet.wikitext): "Dotted and dotless I are distinct letters in Turkish such that ⟨i⟩ becomes ⟨İ⟩ when capitalised, ⟨I⟩ being the capital form of ⟨ı⟩." The Azerbaijani Latin alphabet has the same pair (Wikipedia, "Azerbaijani alphabet", knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/enwiki-Azerbaijani_alphabet.wikitext).

dot_ordinal.source: Azerbaijani writes an ordinal in digits with a period after the digits ("5. sinif"), as Turkish does (Wiktionary, "beşinci" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-tr-beşinci.wikitext): "5'inci, 5.").

joiner.source: CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 25: "iyirmi beş": no conjunction joins the parts of a number.

decimal_marker.source: CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-cardinal renders 2.5 as "iki tam beş"; Wiktionary, "vergül" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-az-vergül.wikitext): "comma".

minus.source: CLDR 48 RBNF az %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of -5: "əksi beş"; Wiktionary, "mənfi" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-az-mənfi.wikitext): "(mathematics) minus (negative quantity)": "mənfi beş dərəcə soyuq", minus five degrees of cold

minus_idioms.source: No idiom puts the minus word before a positive number.

article_one.source: Azerbaijani "bir" is also the indefinite article, as in Turkish (Wikipedia, "Turkish grammar" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Turkish_grammar.wikitext): "The cardinal number bir can be used as an indefinite article").

of.source: No word multiplies a scale word.

fraction_of.source: No word stands between a fraction and a collective.

class_noun.source: No class noun follows a collective.

half_unit.source: The half word comes before the unit ("yarım kilo").

abbreviation.source: No number word is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: The comma is the decimal mark (CLDR 48 az), so ",5" is 0.5.

range_cue.source: Azerbaijani puts "arasında" (between) after the numbers; no word before a range opens it.

digit_suffix_mark.source: Wiktionary, "birinci" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-tr-birinci.wikitext): "1’inci"; Wiktionary, "beşinci" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-tr-beşinci.wikitext): "5'inci": an apostrophe joins a suffix to digits.
